entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, available as managed cloud or Apache-2.0 self-hosted software. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, and a self-hosted server.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight provides long-term agent memory through retain, recall, and reflect operations. It can be deployed with Docker, pip, or Kubernetes and supports hosted and local LLM providers.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that organizes resources, memories, and skills as files. It supports scoped semantic search and session archiving with inspectable Markdown memories.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that structures text into entities, relationships, and searchable chunks. Custom data models, ontologies, plugins, and MCP support let teams connect agents to its knowledge graph engine.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API that extracts conversation facts, reconciles contradictions, and handles automatic forgetting; it is also an official Hermes Agent memory provider. Its connectors include Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, and it processes PDFs, images, videos, and code.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores facts with provenance and supports corrections and withdrawal. It can share memory across agents while keeping transient task state local, with optional semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents and is the upstream library used by the elkimek/honcho-self-hosted Hermes wrapper. It tracks peers across workspaces and sessions, offers Python and TypeScript SDKs, and can run locally or be self-hosted.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git repo, managing a plain Markdown context tree with Git-like commit, branch, and merge operations. It is an official Hermes Agent memory provider with five-tier retrieval, an interactive TUI and REPL, and support for 20 LLM providers.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes agents, described as a zero-dependency, sub-millisecond system with one pure-Python dependency. It integrates through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto extracts and consolidates memories across agents, reconciles conflicting information, and manages forgetting. It also supports memory exchange through the Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that combines vector search with structured facts and includes fabric recall and an auto-curated wiki. Its local infrastructure uses Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, with a Ground Truth hierarchy for prioritizing injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: Autocontext is a recursive self-improving context harness for helping agents succeed on complex tasks. It runs tasks against evaluations, keeps useful lessons while discarding dead ends, and produces traces, reports, and playbooks.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: A Hermes Agent plugin that uses a SQLite store and hierarchical DAG to persist messages. Its lcm_grep and lcm_recall tools help recover details from past context.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Searches session histories from supported coding agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Copilot CLI. You can resume a session or continue it in another agent, with optional semantic recall and no model or server required by default.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: A self-hosted Honcho backend that gives Hermes Agent private memory across sessions. It supports OpenAI-compatible providers and local inference servers, and includes an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: A local-first identity, memory, and secrets layer designed to carry state across supported agents and MCP clients. It connects through hooks, plugins, or extensions and offers a dashboard for browsing memory and asking questions; it can run locally or as a team server.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Provides shared memory for multi-agent systems as plain-text YAML engrams stored on disk. Search works locally after a one-time model download, with keyword fallback; the README reports 95.6% R@5 on LongMemEval-S (N=500).
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: A local-first, on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25, vector search, rank fusion, and cross-encoder reranking. It can generate session handoffs and capture decisions and preferences, with integrations through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Stores long-term agent memory locally in a SQLite file, with FTS5 search and a five-tier schema. Its package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore, without a vector database or embeddings.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: Optimizes context ordering for cache sharing, including text and multimodal context, and provides a context index for reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling. It integrates with Hermes Agent as well as vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and OpenClaw.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: A self-maintaining Hermes memory plugin with an embedded backend by default and an HTTP option. Recall results include a why_retrieved reason, and the plugin supports contradiction tracking and memory canonicalization.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: An agent-driven CLI that proactively recalls and maintains persistent knowledge across sessions. It builds a source-grounded Wiki with citations and history, without requiring embeddings or a vector database.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: Provides long-term, cross-project memory for AI coding agents using inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter as the source of truth. A local DuckDB cache supports hybrid search and retrieval, while MCP servers and host-specific plugins connect it to agents.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: An anticipatory memory system that watches agent session logs to prefetch context. It uses local SQLite-vec storage and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp, and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack combines Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace under a single memory owner, using SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval management. It provides the agent with a purpose-built evidence packet for each query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep builds reflective memory with semantic search, BM25 full-text search, and ranked graph traversal. It can index codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR support, while edge tags connect notes through navigable, bidirectional relationships.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema token use through local keyword-based ranking and supports Tool Search. It integrates as middleware on Hermes 0.19+ without patching Hermes core, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and other listed compatible agents. Its workflows cover migration, handoffs, and memory proposals, with integrations that are opt-in rather than enabled automatically.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes memory plugin stores data in a single embedded .lbdb graph database file and supports BM25 keyword search and named graph relationships. Its importance-weighted recall surfaces high-priority memories during context prefetch.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources, then registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports. It also registers pre_llm_call, on_session_end, and on_session_finalize hooks.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes AgentMemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin with an on-demand summarizer and an audit trace of prefetch operations in trace.jsonl. It supports immediate event deletion, avoiding persistent summaries after deletion.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind recovers the original goal of a long Claude Code or Codex session from its first user turn, skipping tool output and other non-user-turn records. It offers goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes without using a summarizing model or external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: This Hermes memory provider runs inside Hermes and communicates with XMemo over HTTPS for durable cross-session memory with semantic search. It provides ranked, bounded context recall before a turn and includes a local SQLite reliability layer.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Exabase plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It provides tools to search and manually store memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking for retrieval.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, with slash commands for search, file reads, context, and Q&A. It supports Hermes CLI, Telegram, and Hermes Desktop, and includes repository sync and indexed git-history search commands.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with encryption at rest enabled by default. It offers dense HNSW, sparse, and FM-index retrieval, and can run through native Rust FFI or an HTTP daemon.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides memory tools for Hermes Agent, including 17 tools for managing memories and traversing knowledge graphs. Its hybrid search combines BM25, vector, and graph methods, and it can checkpoint context during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit focuses on memory hygiene: it reviews plain Markdown files for stale or conflicting facts and proposes evidence-cited JSON diffs for review. It uses a local Git repository to track and revert changes, without a database.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers provides an agentic skills framework and a software-development workflow that covers specification, planning, and subagent-driven development. Its skills trigger automatically in supported coding-agent harnesses, and the README includes installation instructions for multiple coding agents.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first system for creating and refining interactive web prototypes with a live preview, as well as slide decks, images, and motion graphics. It includes skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins, and supports coding-agent CLIs including Hermes Agent.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project contains 818 structured cybersecurity skills spanning 34 security domains. It maps skills to MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3 frameworks, and is compatible with over 26 AI platforms.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: Drawio-skill turns natural-language prompts and real sources into editable .drawio files. Its incremental sync preserves manual layout and annotations, and it offers the diagramctl CLI with an optional MCP server.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court provides a master router and connector skills, along with vendored copies of official protocol skills. It adds a verification and dispute-resolution layer for agent-to-agent commerce.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: Avoid AI Writing scores files or piped text for detectable AI writing patterns and can rewrite content with up to two editing passes. Its in-place editing mode refuses to modify source code, configuration, or generated data.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw unifies skills across agents and devices, with integrations for Hermes, Codex, Claude Code, and other agents. Its dashboard supports skill management, validation, versioning, and session traces.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills. It supports Claude Code, Codex, and agent-plug-ins.org specifications, and maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This MIT-licensed collection provides 822 professional agent skills that run natively in Hermes Agent and Claude Code, with exports for other assistants. Each skill is a plain-Markdown SKILL.md file containing frameworks, output templates, quality checks, and anti-patterns.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: YouTube Skills provides tools for transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. It supports Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor, and requires a TranscriptAPI key, which has a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: Hermes Skill Factory watches active workflows to detect and propose reusable skills. It can generate SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds, and provides slash commands to manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super Hermes generates custom thinking instructions for specific tasks and includes pre-built analytical lenses for various domains. It reports findings alongside a report of analysis blind spots.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support to Pydantic AI, with progressive disclosure and remote skill registries using Git and S3. It also provides tools for bundled resources and scripts, including sandboxed execution to isolate untrusted scripts from the host.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Creates .lit.md documents that combine prose, diagrams, and source code, then extracts runnable files with a tangler. Edits to those source files can be synced back into the literate document.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design and implementation documents for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes accommodate different project complexity, and a spec review gate evaluates proposals with PASS/FAIL models.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Provides a harness for long-running AI agents with structured memory, cross-feature learning, and a plan-approve-execute workflow. It requires no background service and includes an SLP protocol for supervised teams, plus CLI commands for installation, updates, and diagnostics.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares memory across instances through markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also includes a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: Offers Portuguese-language Hermes Agent skills in SKILL.md format, alongside guides to installation, production, cron, MCP, and skill authoring. The community accepts contributions through pull requests.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides prompting skills for FLUX image and video generation, with BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Lists nine Chainlink skills, each following the Agent Skills specification, for oracle network and smart contract interaction. The README describes the repository as community examples only and gives an npx command for installation.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse, with automated and step-by-step workflows. It also supports skill testing and export.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika uses a workflow language described as “Intent as Code,” with four verbs in one Rust binary. It checks workflows before calling a model, runs with a model you choose, and verifies each run’s tamper-evident record.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with a Python SkilldockClient and CLI. It supports installation with recursive dependency resolution and includes commerce features using TON payments.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Built-in rollback procedures provide a way to recover safely.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This Hermes Agent skill manages Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS with Nextcloud App Passwords and includes a guided setup script for validating credentials and configuring access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: Hermeshub is a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills, with an implementation of the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) v0.9 specification. It also offers federated search across GitHub and Hugging Face and operates autonomously via Hermes Agent on NVIDIA infrastructure.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye narrows the skills presented before LLM calls using five retrieval layers, from hard triggers to semantic embeddings. Its retrieval combines FTS5, synonyms, embeddings, and RRF fusion, and can degrade gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard performs read-only, adversarial code reviews using parallel subagents focused on edge cases, adversarial review, and integration analysis. It combines deterministic pre-scans with tools including semgrep, bandit, eslint, gosec, and ruff, then verifies findings through proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is an ADHD-friendly personal execution system where habits recur and are scored daily, while tasks cover other activities. It runs locally with SQLite, includes an Android client, and connects to agents over MCP.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This Hermes Agent skill simplifies code using parallel Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness agents. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust, and applies changes through a risk-tiered process with an approval gate.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: Hermes Cybersec Lab brings cybersecurity skills, tools, and frameworks together for Hermes Agent, with highlights listing 2,077 skills across multiple repositories and 131+ tools for network, forensics, and exploitation. It also integrates 28 cybersecurity frameworks and standards, including MITRE ATT&CK, MISP, CVSS, EPSS, OWASP, NIST, Sigma, and YARA.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes adapts verified procedures for multi-story task decomposition, requiring evidence-based verification gates. It also provides a systematic investigation protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, plus a Python goal engine for persistent task state management.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: Skillsdotnet implements agentskills.io in C# and .NET, using SKILL.md files for progressive disclosure. It integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading and can automatically register common agent skill directories.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, real-time observability dashboard for tracking token costs, session history, and skill analytics. It uses read-only data access with local log desensitization and offers optional incident alerts via Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: This collection provides plain-markdown agent skills for workflows including code review and session management, with support for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode. Skills can be installed by copying a directory or using the bundled installer.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: This Claude Code skill creates reproducible demo recordings for repository READMEs using VHS tape files or Playwright scripts, and optimizes GIFs to target sizes under 8 MB. It supports terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries, making it a practical choice for adding demos to a range of projects.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: This skill builds Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly to detect field drift, giving skill authors a way to keep their work aligned with changing specs.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: This CLI and MCP server searches a catalog of more than 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills, and provides direct installation commands for discovered tools and plugins. It integrates with MCP-compatible clients including Hermes, Cursor, and Claude Code, helping agents find tools they can use.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: This project analyzes past sessions and installed skills to draft structured improvement proposals for agent skills. Proposals are review-only by default, with auto-apply gated by deterministic, LLM-judge, or regression evaluations.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: These Hermes Agent skills route file operations using environment-specific path syntax and select and verify existing, project-compatible Python interpreters. They support native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, and WSL environments.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Leverage provides skills for social data, web research, and enrichment, alongside packaged skills that combine an agent, skills, and a data flow. It also welcomes community skills in `skills/community/`.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: This collection includes tools to transcribe Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, reduce common Chinese AI writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extract structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. Its focus is practical media and document processing for Hermes.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: This Hermes Agent plugin lets agents browse support bounties, buy ticket context, and submit answers for human review; winning answers are paid in USDC. It also supports creating a bounty board and provides public wallet earnings records.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: This skill automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses using Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Skillseal tests agent skills in isolated Docker containers for structure, functionality, and security. It produces Ed25519-signed certificates and provides a public API for certificate verification and skill submission.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Scavio for Hermes Agent provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server, exposing 191 tools and including five ready-to-use workflow skills. It also supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: AlphaPipeline provides risk checks for token honeypots, tax, and liquidity, alongside market data such as DEX slippage and funding rates. It offers REST endpoints and a remote MCP server for these quantitative risk and slippage checks.
entries.NickSF189/kisscode-agent: This skill helps AI agents join KissCode, with a one-call registration example and SKILL.md and HEARTBEAT.md files. It also lists installation options for several agent platforms and provides a README badge snippet.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This Hermes Agent skill generates structured Chinese news briefings across geographic scales, from global to street level. Reports include core conclusions and action suggestions, and semantic memory uses user interests to expand searches.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This project provides an astrology MCP server for AI agents, with deterministic results and SHA-256 hashes for verification. Its MCP endpoint is available without authentication, and per-call REST payments are supported via x402 or MPP.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: I can’t write a README-grounded description because no README was supplied. The provided highlights alone don’t establish what the project does or why it belongs in this list.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This Nix project packages AI coding agents and development tools, including Hermes, and automatically updates its packages daily. Its README provides `nix run` commands for the listed tools, making it a Nix-based option for running Hermes.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone collects scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. It also documents OpenClaw setup and access to device hardware and UI through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This project provides a Termux installer and guide for running Hermes Agent on Android, using proot-distro Ubuntu. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell commands, and external providers or local models through Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with single-writer safeguards for persistent HERMES_HOME storage. It offers direct and CRD-based deployment workflows, plus configurable gateway mode with optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux and to iOS through iSH. It also supports Telegram voice and file messaging, and scheduled tasks via cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent with hardware-enforced sandboxing through NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and provides configurable policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes. It provides searchable logs, metrics, and alert rules, with access through a REST API, CLI, and MCP server.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image with mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and lets users build specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module supports declarative Hermes deployment, including configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It combines Nix-managed and CLI-installed skills and supports secrets integration through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first web control plane for operating multiple Hermes Agent instances, each with separate workspaces and identities. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular tool, path, and network permission policies.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes-OTG is a portable Hermes Agent package that runs from a USB drive or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles tools for offline use.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project sets up Hermes Gateway as a headless, reboot-safe systemd service on Ubuntu and Debian servers. It also supports autonomous execution of recurring AI cron jobs.
entries.jyje/hermes-agent-helm: This project provides a Helm chart for running Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with installation options via an OCI registry or a published Helm repository. Provider-specific values examples and CI installation on an ephemeral kind cluster make it a deployment option with documented configuration examples and a Kubernetes install check.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a financial trading framework that assigns trading tasks to agents in specialized roles and has them discuss strategies dynamically. It is designed for research purposes.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control is a self-hosted system for governing agent tasks, registrations, memory browsing, and cost tracking. It stands out for offering Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API interfaces, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires provides a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent. It supports persistent tmux sessions, Git worktrees, and multi-repository workspaces, with a web dashboard for structured views, terminal access, and diffs.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: Hermes Agent Control Room is a template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture and task bus support delegation and handoffs, and it includes skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: SwarmClaw is a framework for building autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts provide a way to represent team delegation.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. It combines a Kanban board and live streams of agent reasoning and tool execution with human verification of agent-proposed task completions.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A strict pipeline architecture and Master Orchestrator handle routing and coordination.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for coordinating Leader and Specialist agents through an automated task lifecycle. It integrates MCP and ACP for local tools and communication, with a real-time UI for agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code and orchestrates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations. It also provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator runs an agent-versus-agent arena in which nine autonomous agents operate across two competing AI companies. Using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning, it displays agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics on a real-time dashboard.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel is a local Mixture-of-Agents framework that queries models in parallel and synthesizes their outputs, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, is optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware, and does not require cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a project knowledge graph with `codegraph init`, then auto-syncs it as files change. Its MCP server connects the pre-indexed graph to Hermes Agent and other coding agents, helping reduce token usage and tool calls.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale tracks token consumption across AI coding agents, including Hermes, Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, and Gemini. Its visualization dashboard helps analyze usage across supported clients such as OpenCode and Codex CLI.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap records coding-agent API traffic so you can inspect prompts, tool calls, streaming responses, and token usage. It also lets you compare adjacent requests to see context changes and redacts common auth headers before recording traces.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor is a real-time widget for token usage, costs, and rate limits across 46+ AI coding tools, including Hermes Agent. It also shows historical trends and usage breakdowns, with syncing across multiple devices.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design systems and layout guidance through MCP servers for building UIs with AI. It works with Hermes Agent, Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot, and supports any AI provider that accepts markdown or general prompting.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes is an installable workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent. It includes product-development and operations skills, plus a CTO loop built around seven focused agents.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins is a CLI collection of community and built-in themes for the Hermes terminal UI. Users can create skins with YAML files, and custom skins inherit unspecified values from the default skin.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang statically checks agent-facing content in project directories, including agent configs, tool descriptions, and system prompts. Its findings include file locations and suggested fixes, and it supports CI gates and reviewed baselines.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place provides encrypted agent-to-agent messaging using the Signal Protocol and identity registration with human-readable @handles. It also supports commerce through Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser built for autonomous agent control via MCP, with support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and other AI providers. Its supervisor sidebar manages agent approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads, and it supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel, where it runs natively without a separate process or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages organized around two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin can automatically capture and recall context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating for workflows it says can save 90–99% of tokens, alongside 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research. Automated installation is provided for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md is a framework for creating scoped Hermes agents with per-folder configuration, skills, memories, tools, and custom instructions. It can switch between the default agent and a project-scoped agent.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: This project automates installation of Hermes Agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers ranging from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This tool migrates OpenClaw data—including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives—to Hermes, and maps configurations and credentials to Hermes YAML and JSON formats. It also sets up systemd gateway services and handles nested authentication structures.
entries.observeco/observeco: Observeco is a Hermes plugin that exports real-time telemetry from agent conversations and monitors multi-agent systems in passive or scheduled active-probing modes. It can use local file changes to establish config-aware baselines for detecting performance drift.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: Hermes Voice adds voice interaction with wake-word support, adaptive turn-taking, and barge-in capabilities. It runs offline without API keys or accounts and supports 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: Hermes Startup provides a deterministic local runtime that operates with zero network access by default. It requires explicit approval for consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: This Hermes memory plugin supports semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage, with tools to search, add, and delete memories. It also includes a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: CC-Switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other agent tools, including Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI. It lets users switch API providers in one click and manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with a built-in agent that does not require a separate CLI installation. It also includes 21 built-in professional assistants and supports macOS, Windows, and Linux.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI provides browser access to Hermes Agent, including from a phone. Its three-panel interface brings together sessions, chat, and workspace files, with controls for profiles, models, and workspaces.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: Hermes Desktop is a desktop companion for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent, using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI manages profiles, sessions, skills, and tools, and the app is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: Ekko Studio is a web dashboard for Hermes Agent that brings together chats, sessions, agent integrations, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration. It also supports visual workflows with schedules and approval gates, and is available as a desktop app, npm CLI, or Docker image.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: Hermes Workspace is a web workspace combining chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector panel. Its features include Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: Codeg is a collaborative coding workspace that aggregates sessions from Hermes and other agents, including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, as a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, delegate across agents, or queue to-dos in worktrees.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This native Mac workspace connects directly to Hermes hosts locally or over SSH and provides views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs. An embedded terminal offers direct shell access and system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent, with support for Windows and macOS. It includes a built-in Hermes-CN-Core kernel with health checks and updates, alongside interfaces for chat, memory management, and LaTeX and Markdown rendering.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects the active browser context to a local or remote Hermes Agent runtime, including Hermes Cloud and self-hosted connections. Its Bot Mode supports agent switching and group chats; Hermes Control is opt-in and Chromium-only.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: Hermex is a native SwiftUI iPhone app for driving a self-hosted Hermes agent, paired with a hermes-webui server. It supports streaming chats and file or image attachments, and lets users browse, search, and resume sessions and view scheduled tasks, skills, memory, and insights.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: Wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, as well as custom LLM model routing. Its runtime dashboard tracks token usage and latency, while a live workspace monitors code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is an interactive TUI for monitoring agent activity, with nine tabs and four selectable color themes. It tracks agent growth, git projects, and scheduled cron jobs, and includes a tmux operator view for managing live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: This native macOS session browser covers Hermes agents and other coding-agent CLIs, with search across prompts, responses, tool activity, errors, and file paths. It can resume supported sessions in Terminal.app, iTerm2, or Warp, and shows per-session Codex and Claude quota burn.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: This self-hosted web dashboard brings Hermes stack controls into a browser, including a terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status panel. Its real-time chat visualizes tool calls, while an MCP control plane and ZOO Swarm Monitor cover server lifecycles, agent health, and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: This native macOS workspace runs Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud computers and SSH hosts. It offers one-click automated installation on fresh cloud computers and integrated WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: This self-hostable mission-control dashboard template connects a local Hermes agent with web dashboards through a Postgres message bus. An approval inbox handles requests with side effects; the project is built with Next.js 16, React 19, Prisma, and Tailwind CSS v4.
entries.liftaris/herm: Herm is an alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard built with OpenTUI for chatting and managing agent sessions. It also combines a kanban board for agentic work with controls for profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: This locally running React SPA is a mobile-first dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. Its terminal chat supports streaming responses and file attachments, while dual HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519 authentication validates Telegram and background spawning supports five concurrent agent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: Portable Hermes Agent provides a dark-themed Windows desktop GUI with multilingual support and session management. It includes workflow automation and runtime tool creation, and supports local models through LM Studio.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: This self-hosted Hermes interface pairs a glassmorphic chat experience with real-time log streaming. Its file browser and task-tracking dashboard sit alongside tools for managing skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI is a monitoring and configuration dashboard with real-time session activity and cost tracking. It also allows inspection of conversation histories and skill source code, while configuration and environment variables are monitored read-only.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: Pan UI is a self-hosted, chat-first workspace for AI, with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards. Its marketplace helps users discover and install skills and MCP servers, while isolated profiles keep sessions, memory, and API keys separate.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: This native desktop client supports multi-agent Hermes workflows, including collaboration between 20 specialized AI agents and a PM orchestrator. It pairs streaming SSE chat and model switching with a visual Skill Store offering 50+ curated one-click installations.
entries.nicolasestrem/hermes-model-switcher: Hermes Model Switcher lets you compare configured model routes across profiles in one matrix and switch between them from the Hermes Agent Web Dashboard. It previews changes before applying them and includes named presets and a guarded Undo.
entries.robbyczgw-cla/hermes-ui-plus: Hermes UI Plus is an interactive chat client for a self-hosted Hermes Agent, with command approvals, live tool-step updates, and answer cards for checklists, choices, forms, rankings, and votes. It runs on Android, web, and macOS, with a Linux alpha.
